cues.en: Maybe we can improve on these results somehow by tweaking the parameters of the algorithm.
cues.zh: 也許調整演算法參數，就能改善結果。

cues.en: As an exercise, try out the different similarity measures SurpriseLib offers.
cues.zh: 作為練習，試試 SurpriseLib 提供的不同相似度衡量方式。

cues.en: Right now we're using cosine, but how about msd and Pearson?
cues.zh: 目前使用 cosine，那 msd 和 Pearson 呢？

cues.en: Give it a go, and compare the results you get from each.
cues.zh: 試試看，比較各自結果。

cues.en: Are they substantially different?
cues.zh: 有明顯差異嗎？

cues.en: After you've experimented with these different metrics, continue to the next slide and I'll show you my results.
cues.zh: 實驗過不同指標後，繼續下一張投影片，會展示我的結果。

cues.en: So I tabulated my results in using different similarity metrics with KNN for both the user-based and item-based cases.
cues.zh: 我整理了使用者式與項目式 KNN，採用不同相似度指標的結果。

cues.en: Let's start with user-based.
cues.zh: 先看使用者式。

cues.en: If we look at the RMSE error scores, we might conclude that mean squared distance, or msd, significantly outperforms the cosine metric, it's .97 as opposed to .99.
cues.zh: 看 RMSE 誤差分數，可能會認為均方距離，也就是 MSD，明顯勝過餘弦：0.97 對 0.99。

cues.en: But look at the actual top N recommendations for our test user, they are exactly the same.
cues.zh: 但看測試使用者的實際 Top-N 推薦，完全相同。

cues.en: This means the math behind msd leads to more accurate rating predictions, but the ranking of those predictions is more or less the same.
cues.zh: 這表示 MSD 背後的數學，讓評分預測更準確，但預測的排序大致相同。

cues.en: So from a practical standpoint, that increased accuracy doesn't matter.
cues.zh: 因此，實務上，準確程度的提升沒有影響。

cues.en: I just can't say enough that focusing on accuracy alone is not a good idea.
cues.zh: 我真的要一再強調，只專注準確程度不是好主意。

cues.en: You need to look at real-world outputs of the system together with it.
cues.zh: 必須一起看系統在真實世界的輸出。

cues.en: Pearson at least delivers some slightly different results, but are they better?
cues.zh: Pearson 至少產生略為不同的結果，但有比較好嗎？

cues.en: Well not according to the RMSE score, although in theory Pearson is supposed to normalize things in such a way that should be beneficial.
cues.zh: 根據 RMSE，沒有，儘管理論上 Pearson 應該用有益的方式將資料正規化。

cues.en: Is Othello a better top recommendation than One Magic Christmas?
cues.zh: 把 Othello 當第一推薦，比 One Magic Christmas 更好嗎？

cues.en: Well for me, it certainly would be.
cues.zh: 對我來說，當然是。

cues.en: So again, what the accuracy metric is telling you might run counter to what real-world users might respond to.
cues.zh: 因此，準確程度指標傳達的訊息，可能再次與真實使用者的反應相反。

cues.en: It's a similar story looking at item-based KNN.
cues.zh: 項目式 KNN 也有類似情況。

cues.en: No matter what the similarity metric, we end up with a lot of obscure movies, many of them foreign.
cues.zh: 不管哪個相似度指標，最後都有很多冷門電影，其中許多是外國片。

cues.en: And there's an even bigger difference between cosine and msd's RMSE scores, yet they produce exactly the same results.
cues.zh: 而且，cosine 與 MSD 的 RMSE 差距更大，產生的結果卻完全相同。

cues.en: Pearson fares better on RMSE in the item-based case, and it also generates a set of recommendations that is substantially different.
cues.zh: Pearson 在項目式情況下，RMSE 表現更好，也產生一組明顯不同的推薦。

cues.en: Subjectively, I recognize at least a couple of these recommendations as ones I might enjoy.
cues.zh: 主觀上，至少認得其中幾個，是我可能會喜歡的電影。

cues.en: So this tells me that in a real world setting, experimenting with Pearson similarity on an item-based collaborative filtering may be a worthwhile experiment.
cues.zh: 這告訴我，在真實世界，對項目式協同過濾實驗 Pearson 相似度，也許值得。

cues.en: SurpriseLib also offers some variants on KNN recommendations that we can try as well.
cues.zh: SurpriseLib 還提供一些 KNN 推薦的變形，也可以嘗試。

cues.en: I evaluated them on the item-based case just to see if any of them produced markedly better results.
cues.zh: 我用項目式情況評估它們，看看是否有任何一個能產生明顯更好的結果。

cues.en: The short answer is no.
cues.zh: 簡短答案是，沒有。

cues.en: Although on paper they appear to have much better accuracy results, the top-N results are still pretty obscure and random.
cues.zh: 雖然理論上的準確程度結果好得多，Top-N 結果仍然相當冷門、隨機。

cues.en: This should be expected because each of these algorithms attempt to somehow baseline their rating predictions to be more consistent with how the real ratings are distributed in our training data.
cues.zh: 這是可以預期的，因為每個演算法都試圖用某種方式，讓評分預測以基準校正，更符合訓練資料中真實評分的分布。

cues.en: Without getting too far into the details, the baseline variant predicts ratings relative to some baseline average rating score across the data set.
cues.zh: 不深入細節，Baseline 變形會相對於資料集的某個基準平均評分，預測評分。

cues.en: And the means and z score variants attempt to account for differences in the baselines for individual users, like we described when we talked about the adjusted cosine metric.
cues.zh: 而 Means 與 ZScore 變形，試圖補償個別使用者基準的差異，就像談調整式餘弦時描述的。

cues.en: In every case, you can see that we did in fact achieve better accuracy scores.
cues.zh: 每種情況都能看到，確實得到更好的準確程度分數。

cues.en: But the end results don't care about accuracy.
cues.zh: 但最終結果不在乎準確程度。

cues.en: They only care about the order of the predicted ratings we end up with.
cues.zh: 只在乎最後預測評分的順序。

cues.en: So, we're left with recommendations that don't seem all that inspiring again.
cues.zh: 因此，最後的推薦，再次顯得不太令人振奮，

cues.en: Even if the accuracy metrics look exciting.
cues.zh: 即使準確程度指標看起來很令人興奮。

cues.en: So why does KNN have so much trouble presenting compelling items to users?
cues.zh: 為什麼 KNN 很難提供讓使用者感興趣的項目？

cues.en: Well, it's actually pretty well known that KNN doesn't work well in practice, and unfortunately some people conclude that collaborative filtering in general is some naive approach that should be replaced with
cues.zh: 其實，KNN 實務表現不佳，是相當知名的問題。不幸的是，有些人因此認為整個協同過濾都是天真的方法，應該用

cues.en: completely different techniques.
cues.zh: 完全不同的技術取代。

cues.en: But as we've seen, collaborative filtering isn't the problem, it's forcing collaborative filtering to make rating predictions that's the problem.
cues.zh: 但如前所見，問題不在協同過濾，而在於強迫它預測評分。

cues.en: Remember back when we started this section?
cues.zh: 記得這一節剛開始嗎？

cues.en: We had some pretty exciting results when we just focused on making top-N recommendations and completely forgot about optimizing for rating accuracy.
cues.zh: 當時只專注於 Top-N 推薦，完全不管最佳化評分準確程度，就得到相當令人興奮的結果。

cues.en: And, it turns out that's what's at the heart of the problem.
cues.zh: 而這正是問題核心。

cues.en: Ratings are not continuous in nature, and KNN treats them as though they are continuous values that can be predicted on a continuous scale.
cues.zh: 評分本質上不是連續的，但 KNN 卻把它當成能在連續尺度上預測的連續值。

cues.en: If you really wanted to go with KNN, it would be more appropriate to treat it as a rating classification problem than as a rating prediction problem.
cues.zh: 如果真的想使用 KNN，把它當成評分分類問題，會比評分預測問題更合適。

cues.en: KNN is also very sensitive to sparse data, so in all fairness you might get better results if you didn't just have 100,000 ratings to play with.
cues.zh: KNN 對稀疏資料也很敏感，所以公平地說，如果不只十萬筆評分可用，也許會有更好結果。

cues.en: But the most fundamental thing is that accuracy isn't everything.
cues.zh: 但最根本的是，準確程度不是一切。

cues.en: The main reason KNN produces underwhelming results is because it's trying to solve the wrong problem.
cues.zh: KNN 結果令人失望的主因，是它試圖解決錯誤的問題。
